161 Mrs Greene to move—That the House:—
Notes:—

the 2026 report of the Interim Commissioner for Children and Young People, ‘“You’ve got nothing else to do…” Making Isolation Less Harmful: Views from Young People at Ashley Youth Detention Centre’; and
that between January and April 2026:—
there were between 15 and 21 young people detained at Ashley Youth Detention Centre on any given day;
more than 80 per cent were on remand;
at least one in three were Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander;
young people were isolated far more often because of operational staff shortages than for behavioural reasons;
in January there were an average of 74 operational staff shortage isolation events per young person, compared with 15 behavioural isolation events;
operational staff shortage isolation continued to occur daily in April, at an average of 37 events per young person; and
5,467 operational staff shortage isolation events were recorded during the reporting period.

Acknowledges the report identifies a pattern of isolation arising from operational constraints, including low staffing, shift transitions and competing staff demands, rather than the behaviour of young people.
Further notes that staffing shortages can restrict access to education, programs and meaningful activities, increasing frustration and the risk of further behavioural escalation.

Calls on the Rockliff Government to urgently address staffing and operational constraints at Ashley Youth Detention Centre so young people are not routinely isolated because there are insufficient staff available to safely operate the Centre. (9 September 2026)
162 Mr Vermey to move—That the House:—
Acknowledges that aged care is a federal responsibility.
Notes that, on any given day, approximately 78 Tasmanians remain stranded in public hospitals awaiting aged care placement.
Calls on the Commonwealth Government to provide immediate, medium, and longer term solutions to address this growing crisis. (9 September 2026)
